name: How Much Budget Should You Set Aside for Remodel Surprises?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I keep for a Los Angeles County kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I keep for a Los Angeles County kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency is the amount you set aside for surprises that are likely in a remodel but not fully known at bidding time. For a kitchen renovation, that can include damaged subflooring, outdated wiring, plumbing corrections, framing issues, or finish upgrades made after selections are finalized. In Los Angeles County, older homes and layout changes often increase the need for a contingency. A practical planning range is often 10% to 20% of the total project budget, but the right amount depends on the age of the home and the amount of demolition involved. If the project is highly customized or the existing kitchen has signs of leaks, patchwork repairs, or deferred maintenance, a larger reserve is safer. Ask the contractor which issues they commonly uncover in similar homes and whether the estimate already includes allowances for likely unknowns. The goal is to avoid stopping work when the first surprise appears. A well-planned contingency gives you flexibility without derailing the schedule or forcing rushed decisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency is 10% to 20% of the project budget, with higher reserves for older homes or projects that change the layout. The contingency covers hidden damage, code updates, and material upgrades. If a contractor says no contingency is needed, the estimate may be too optimistic.
